content.text:
The feature fits the existing ports/services/Postgres structure. The missing pieces are stable search-result identity, an entity-details service/repository, HTTP detail routes, and routed frontend views.

Current flow:

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  App["App.svelte search effect"] --> Client["search.ts /api/search"]
  Client --> Proxy["Vite strips /api"]
  Proxy --> HTTP["GET /search handler"]
  HTTP --> Service["entity_search::Service"]
  Service --> MP["ParliamentMemberRepo"]
  Service --> Funder["FunderRepo"]
  MP --> DB["ExposedDatabase / SQLx macros"]
  Funder --> DB
```

Relevant pointers:

- `frontend/src/App.svelte:40`: debounced, cancellable search effect. `:315` renders a static result row; name is a span at `:317`.
- `frontend/src/lib/search.ts:19`: frontend `Entity` contains name/kind/funder kind only. `:62` calls the API.
- `frontend/vite.config.ts:4`: `/api` proxy targets port 6999 and strips `/api`.
- `exposed/src/lib/inbound/http/routes.rs:10`: only `/search` exists.
- `exposed/src/lib/inbound/http/handlers.rs:45`: `SearchEntity` DTO drops identity; `:72` converts request, calls service, maps errors.
- `exposed/src/lib/domain/services/entity_search.rs:47`: queries MPs then funders, merging descending similarity. Limit applies independently to each type.
- `exposed/src/lib/outbound/parliament_member.rs:43`: search SQL returns Parliament numeric ID, party and constituency, but not member UUID.
- `exposed/src/lib/outbound/funder.rs:22`: search SQL omits funder UUID; selected company number is discarded.
- `exposed/src/lib/domain/models/funder.rs:7`: `Funder` currently contains only name/kind.
- `exposed/src/lib/domain/models/parliament_member.rs:5`: MP contains numeric Parliament ID, party and constituency.
- `exposed/src/lib/inbound/http/state.rs:9` and `server.rs:49`: state currently contains one search service; server constructs it with two clones of the database.

Data contracts and pitfalls:

- `db/migrations/20260915000000_initial.up.sql:15`: members have internal UUID plus unique numeric Parliament ID. Choose one explicit public identity; do not derive routes from names.
- Baseline `:90`: funders have UUID identity, **exact-name** uniqueness, nullable status/company number. This is not resolved real-world entity identity: aliases split, identical source names merge.
- Baseline `:106`: funding rows join declarations through `source_declaration_id`; declarations join members through internal `member_id`.
- `ingest/src/exposed/adapters/declaration_postgres.py:58`: duplicate funding rows are deliberately preserved. `Counter` comparison recognizes multiplicity; do not `DISTINCT` financial rows or count declarations after a fanout join.
- Same file `:74`: changed declaration funding replaces all payment rows. Funding UUIDs are not stable across source corrections, whereas declaration ID and funder identity remain suitable links.
- Amount is nullable PostgreSQL `NUMERIC`; currency is nullable text. Preserve exact decimal values as strings in JSON, group totals by currency, and expose unknown amounts/currencies rather than treating missing values as zero or GBP.
- `registration_date` is nullable and stored at midnight UTC (`baseline:79`). Recent declarations should sort registration date descending with nulls last and a deterministic source ID tie-breaker. Fetch/audit dates are not declaration dates.
- Only latest selected declaration publication is stored; Rust selects published date then register ID (`outbound/declaration_source.rs:131`). This is not an append-only history of amendments.
- Members’ party data is latest stored metadata; upsert overwrites it (`outbound/parliament_member.rs:106`). Party totals therefore represent recipients grouped by their stored party, not necessarily party when funding was declared. Label that limitation.
- Payment type can describe support received by a party organisation rather than personal cash; existing README examples explain this. Prefer “declared support” wording for totals.
- Some declarations have no financial entries, and some entries have no funder. MP declarations require an outer join/grouped assembly to retain both.
- Existing extra migration `db/migrations/20261002203727_rm_terms.up.sql:3` drops term/service tables despite baseline still creating them. Do not rely on those tables for historical party attribution.

Verification setup:

```sh
npm --prefix frontend ci
npm --prefix frontend run check
npm --prefix frontend run build
npm --prefix frontend run format:check
cd frontend
PLAYWRIGHT_BROWSERS_PATH=0 npx playwright install chromium
npm test
```

Playwright starts Vite on `127.0.0.1:4173`; existing tests mock API responses. Add navigation/back/direct-link/loading/error coverage and genuine backend smoke checks separately.

```sh
cargo fmt --all --check
cargo test --package exposed --lib
cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings
cargo run --package exposed --bin exposed -- server
curl 'http://127.0.0.1:6999/search?term=John&max_entries=10&strictness=1'
```

Rust SQLx macros need `DATABASE_URL` and a compatible live schema at compile time; no `.sqlx` cache exists. `.env.example` uses host PostgreSQL port 55432. Existing repository tests use `#[sqlx::test]`, migrations and fixtures to create isolated databases. HTTP integration tests start an ephemeral listener but use configured database (`exposed/tests/common/mod.rs`). Server falls back to an ephemeral port if 6999 is occupied; inspect its printed port before setting `EXPOSED_API_ORIGIN`.

README mentions `make` targets, but no Makefile exists in this checkout. Use explicit commands until that discrepancy is resolved. Compose project is globally named `exposed`; running its full stack from this worktree can recreate shared containers, so isolate runtime configuration when checking the new backend.
